### OSI model (text)  {.smaller}

<table>
<tr><td>7</td><td>application</td><td>what requests/etc.</td></tr>
<tr><td>6</td><td>presentation</td><td>format of data</td></tr>
<tr><td>5</td><td>session</td><td>coordinate multiple streams</td></tr>
<tr><td>4</td><td>transport</td><td>streams of data</td></tr>
<tr><td>3</td><td>network</td><td>message to correct network</td></tr>
<tr><td>2</td><td>data link</td><td rowspawn="2">message to correct machine<br>message into bits/symbols</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td></td></tr>

</table>
 

* internet: usually combines layers 7/6/5


### OSI model  {.smaller}


* standardized by ISO (International Standards Organization) and ITU (International Telecommunications Union)
* full set of protocols\ldots 

   * file transfer, message sending, directory lookups \ldots

* that were often implemented and sometimes used\ldots
* but mostly lost out to IETF-standardized Internet protocols 

   * Internet Engineering Task Force



### OSI influence (1) 


* term ‘layer 7’, ‘layer 4’, ‘layer 3’, etc. almost always refer to OSI model
* ...even though most of Internet does not follow it 

   * early Internet protocols predate OSI



### OSI influence (2)  {.smaller}


* are a lot of Internet protocols influenced by OSI protocols
* OSI's DAP (directory access protocol)  

   * adapted into IETF's LDAP (lightweight directory access protocol)

* OSI presentation layer ASN.1 used in\ldots 

   * telephony (between telephone companies)
   * inter-bank messaging
   * lots of cryptography-related protocols
   * \ldots

* OSI's routing protocol IS-IS still common in large Internet-connected networks 

   * (adapted to work alongside IETF protocols)



### Internet layers  {.smaller}

\small <table>
<tr><td>OSI layer</td><td>name</td><td>examples</td><td>purpose</td></tr>
<tr><td>\hline 7</td><td>application</td><td>HTTP, SSH,</td><td>application-defined meanings</td></tr>
<tr><td>&nbsp;</td><td>&nbsp;</td><td>SMTP, DNS, \ldots</td><td>&nbsp;</td></tr>
<tr><td>\hline 4</td><td>transport</td><td>TCP, UDP, \ldots</td><td>reach correct program,\linebreak reliablity/streams</td></tr>
<tr><td>\hline 3</td><td>network</td><td>IPv4, IPv6, \ldots</td><td>reach correct machine\linebreak(across networks)</td></tr>
<tr><td>\hline 2</td><td>link</td><td>Ethernet, Wi-Fi, \ldots</td><td>coordinate shared wire/radio</td></tr>
<tr><td>\hline 1</td><td>physical</td><td>\ldots</td><td>encode bits for wire/radio</td></tr>
<tr><td>\hline</td></tr>
</table>
